## 0. Executive summary
<!-- enc:block:01M4JCQ2D99ZS5WK406TG66PE9 -->

**The ask.** Accept this BRD as the next-generation architecture vision for io's four web stacks (DVP-FTR-098 AC4). Acceptance locks 16 decisions (section 3.2), two of them io's rulings of 2026-10-10 (L-15 Keycloak stays on vagamod with kit parity; L-16 stack order coach, think, enceladus, vagamod), and lets the coordination lead file the records proposed in section 8. The 11 deferred decisions (section 3.3) stay open and do not block wave E0. [INF]

**The decision.** Every action an agent can take through an MCP surface becomes possible for io in that stack's UI, enforced by a CI parity check per stack [DOC: DOC-5132058DFFAB s1]. The UI is built from one versioned kit package per design area, pinned per stack; an improvement ships as one kit bump plus one PR per stack [DOC: DOC-5132058DFFAB s3]. This BRD folds 24 audit, research and reconciliation documents into one program: one capability manifest feeding navigation, forms and the parity check; one server-enforced dry_run/execute policy table; one gate hub; six waves. [INF]

**Five numbers that matter.**
1. **220** MCP actions across 7 surfaces and 4 stacks [DOC: DOC-04829C0677A3 s1].
2. **34 covered / 11 partial / 175 missing** (15% covered): Enceladus 14/105, think 14/103, vagamod 6/12 [DOC: DOC-408DB108D7B9 s3].
3. **129** actions (Enceladus v2 105, io-graph 24) have no per-action schema until an unwrapped action registry ships; this is the program's first implementation dependency [DOC: DOC-3724FD572867 s2].
4. **91** actions on five surfaces already serve per-tool JSON Schema and can be covered as soon as the shell palette and schema_form kits ship [DOC: DOC-3724FD572867 s2].
5. **10** packages (eight areas plus tokens and parity), released from one kit repo to a private CodeArtifact scope, which five inputs recommend [INF].

**The central call: parity before polish.** The cheapest route to parity is generic. The shell turns every unmapped capability into a palette command that opens a form generated from the action's contract [DOC: DOC-6F606A034072 s3.1]. Waves therefore run E0 foundation and unwrapped registry, E1 auth and shell, E2 schema_form generic coverage, E3 md/search/feed, E4 gates and recipes, E5 uplift. vagamod reaches full parity first, then think's schema-ready surfaces, then Enceladus once unwrapped. Bespoke pages follow as UX work. [INF]

**What happens next.** On acceptance, the coordination lead stamps evidence on DVP-TSK-828 and files section 8. E0 starts with the kit repo and registry, the caps.json generators and unwrapped registries, and the parity check in report-only mode against the committed baseline. On rejection, section 10 lists the decisions to revisit. [INF]

**Amendments (io, 2026-10-10).** A1: ai.vagamod.io keeps Keycloak; the kit documents and, as the target, supports Keycloak feature parity including multi-tenancy, so vagamod can be hosted for external tenants. A2: program stack order is coach.thepup.io first (modernization prelude to DOC-8EDA2CBF674E), then think.thepup.io, then enceladus.jreese.net, then ai.vagamod.io. Everything else is accepted as written. [DOC: io]

## 1. North-star parity acceptance criterion

**Invariant.** Any action an agent can execute through an MCP surface can be executed by a human through that stack's UI [DOC: DOC-5132058DFFAB s1]. Formally: for each surface S and each action A in S.capabilities, there is a UI route or command R where R.handler == A.handler. The evidence is that `diff(capabilities_registry, ui_route_manifest)` is empty. A CI check in each stack enforces this, not a reviewer's opinion. [DOC: DOC-5132058DFFAB s1]

**Enforcement shape** [DOC: DOC-408DB108D7B9 s4], adopted with one reconciliation (see the last item, and L-03 and L-04):

```yaml
parity_check:
  inputs:
    inventory: "parity/inventory.json per MCP surface, generated from the surface registry or tools/list; fields action, rw, via, flag"   # DOC-408DB108D7B9 s4
    route_manifest: "parity/routes.yaml per stack, generated (enceladus: frontend/ui-v2 TanStack route tree + handler grep; vagamod: app-router pages + hook fetches; think: frontend/pwa views using mcp:<action>/execute:<action>; coach: none while it fronts no MCP surface)"   # DOC-408DB108D7B9 s4
    mapping: "parity/map.yaml: action -> {handler | waiver: {reason, owner, expires}}"   # DOC-408DB108D7B9 s4
    baseline: "parity/baseline.json committed counts for a ratchet"   # DOC-408DB108D7B9 s4
  checks:   # DOC-408DB108D7B9 s4
    - every inventory action has a mapping entry or an explicit waiver
    - every mapped handler exists in the generated route manifest
    - covered count per stack and per surface never drops below baseline
    - waivers past expiry fail
    - "nav items with status: planned past 30 days fail"   # INF, from DOC-6F606A034072 D9
  output: "PARITY-FAIL <stack> <surface> <action> <unmapped|stale-handler|regressed|waiver-expired>; per-stack summary 'covered X/T partial Y missing Z (baseline X0/T)'; non-zero exit on any finding"   # DOC-408DB108D7B9 s4
  reconciliation: "inventory.json, the shell CapabilityManifest (DOC-6F606A034072 s3.1) and ActionRegistry.manifest() (DOC-3724FD572867 s1.1) are ONE artifact, caps.json, generated by the MCP adapter build from the governed handler registry"   # INF; owner rule from DOC-93597FD399C6 D8
  rollout: "report-only in E0, blocking with ratchet from E1, blocking at zero-missing per stack when that stack reaches 'done' (section 7)"   # INF
```

**Today's baseline** [DOC: DOC-408DB108D7B9 s3]:

```yaml
baseline_2026_10_10:
  all_stacks: {covered: 34, partial: 11, missing: 175, total: 220}
  enceladus.jreese.net: {covered: 14, partial: 6, missing: 85, total: 105, without_flag_gated: "14/6/65 of 85"}
  ai.vagamod.io: {covered: 6, partial: 4, missing: 2, total: 12}
  think.thepup.io: {covered: 14, partial: 1, missing: 88, total: 103}
  coach.thepup.io: {covered: 0, partial: 0, missing: 0, total: 0, note: "fronts no MCP surface"}
```

**One definitional gap this BRD closes.** The invariant does not say whether a generic schema_form behind a palette command counts as "covered". This BRD rules that it does. The command calls the same governed handler through the same execute path, so it satisfies R.handler == A.handler. Bespoke pages are UX work and are tracked separately from parity. [INF; see L-05 and section 10 Q-01]

Synthesis [INF]:
- No stack wins outright in any area except md (think's engine) and shell (Enceladus' chassis). Every Wave C doc picked a composite best-of-breed [DOC: DOC-FB1738F8E0A2, DOC-6F606A034072, DOC-488491DADD6C, DOC-0048EA99B6DD, DOC-256B5F36C6FD s2].

- Enceladus' gap is mostly hidden behind wrappers.
- vagamod is nearly done: 2 missing and 4 partial.

## 3. Vision: the next generation of io's software and cloud architecture ecosystem
<!-- enc:block:01M4JCRJ3S3Q0YDM6Y5E5CT6VJ -->

### 3.1 The ecosystem as a whole

The next generation of io's estate has one rule: **a governed handler is the only place an action exists.** [INF] Everything else adapts that handler:
- The MCP adapter exposes it to agents.
- The UI route or palette command exposes it to io.
- The recipe step sequences it.
- The gate holds a proposed call to it until a human clears it.

Because humans and agents call the same handler, they get the same validation, the same dry run, the same policy check and the same audit trail. That is what "parity" means in substance, not just in route count [INF; the handler-equality form is from DOC-5132058DFFAB s1].

**Stacks.** Four stacks deploy independently, each from its own domain and pipeline [DOC: DOC-5132058DFFAB s2, s6]:
- enceladus.jreese.net is the governance and operations plane. It is mature and enhanced in place.
- ai.vagamod.io is the vagamod product. It keeps its own IdP, Keycloak, behind an adapter [DOC: DOC-FB1738F8E0A2 s3].
- think.thepup.io is the primary new-build host for every non-Enceladus io surface: io-graph, io-finance, io-travel, io-devops and chosen-family [DOC: DOC-5132058DFFAB s2].
- coach.thepup.io fronts no MCP surface today [DOC: DOC-408DB108D7B9 s3]. It is a kit consumer and has donated contracts (auth authz, feed wire, shell frame). It joins parity only when it gains a surface. [INF]

Repos may stay separate. The invariant is the package boundary per design area [DOC: DOC-5132058DFFAB s2].

**Surfaces and the manifest.** Each MCP surface publishes `caps.json` at build time [INF; owner rule from DOC-93597FD399C6 D8]. The build generates it from the governed handler registry. Each entry carries the per-action input and output schema, MCP annotations (readOnly, destructive, idempotent, openWorld), whether a governance hash is required, and the flag state. This one artifact feeds four things [INF]:
- shell navigation, through `defineNavRegistry({fromCapabilities})`;
- the schema_form registry;
- the parity inventory;
- the auth policy table's action keys.

The Wave C docs had three similar manifests (shell CapabilityManifest, ActionRegistry.manifest(), parity inventory.json). This BRD makes them one [INF].

**The kit.** Ten packages live under one `@io-kit` scope:
- eight area packages: auth, shell, md, search, feed, schema_form, recipes, gates;
- two supporting packages: tokens, consumed by shell [DOC: DOC-6F606A034072 s3.2], and parity, which provides the CI checker and conformance schemas [DOC: DOC-408DB108D7B9 s4 placement].

The kit is TypeScript-first and ships `.d.ts` files for the JS stacks think and coach [DOC: DOC-1C29BA594950 D2; INF lock]. Each package has a framework-free core, a React adapter and a `/testing` conformance subpath. Server-side subpaths (`@io-kit/auth/server`) run in the Lambdas, so the same policy code executes on both sides of the wire [DOC: DOC-FB1738F8E0A2 s3].

**Cloud.** The cloud side stays AWS-native, with documented exit costs [INF]:
- Cognito: one shared pool for the three Cognito stacks, with Keycloak for vagamod.
- Lambda handlers behind CloudFront, plus a per-stack auth edge at `/auth/*` that does code exchange and refresh with an HttpOnly cookie [DOC: DOC-D484594E8479 s4].
- AppSync Events for realtime, carrying signals only. Data always comes from the governed HTTP handler [DOC: DOC-256B5F36C6FD s3.1].
- DynamoDB for feed sequence numbers, recipe runs and the hash-chained gate decision log [DOC: DOC-6E3844E7EBBD D1; DOC-1931CDD35AAA headline via DOC-18973FB09747].
- CodeArtifact for the kit registry.
- The docstore for recipe definitions [DOC: DOC-BE6CCB537BCF D1].

**How an improvement propagates.** Suppose a fix lands in `@io-kit/search` [DOC: DOC-5132058DFFAB s3; INF mechanics]:
1. It passes the package's own tests and the conformance suite run against every consumer's recorded fixtures.
2. A changeset releases a minor version to CodeArtifact.
3. A bot opens one PR per stack that pins the new version.
4. Each PR runs that stack's contract tests and parity check, and each stack merges on its own schedule.

A breaking bump for one stack therefore blocks only that stack's PR, never the other three [DOC: DOC-5132058DFFAB s6 coupling mitigation].

**What io can do without agent compute.** At the end state io can, from any stack's UI [INF]:
- run any of the 220 actions through a generated form, with a dry run that shows the resolved call, the principal, the governance hash and the side-effect count before executing [DOC: DOC-3724FD572867 s1];
- start a recipe and run it to the next human gate [DOC: DOC-BE6CCB537BCF s1];
- clear any decision card in one inbox that spans every project, where the exact call fires on clear [DOC: DOC-C1A8ABB466FD s4; DOC-1931CDD35AAA];
- read every docstore document with its conventions rendered [DOC: DOC-488491DADD6C].

Agents become an accelerator, not a dependency. This is the DVP-FTR-098 user story satisfied literally.

**Beyond convergence.** The stage-2 and stage-3 tracks in Wave B are a separate, later program, not this one [DOC: DOC-5132058DFFAB s6 scope_creep]. Examples include Cedar policies, passkeys, durable-function recipe runners, View Transitions, Shiki, Bedrock rerank, signed plan/apply and Web Push gates [DOC: DOC-D484594E8479, DOC-93597FD399C6, DOC-C97D5B581CB4, DOC-1C29BA594950, DOC-A4F0A2A44AE2, DOC-24F0950D339A, DOC-6E3844E7EBBD, DOC-C1A8ABB466FD s4]. The kit's seams are designed to absorb them. Examples: Cedar replaces the policy table behind `authorize()`, and the durable runner replaces DynamoDB behind the recipes HTTP handlers. [INF]

### 3.2 Locked decisions

"Locked" means one of two things: the program brief already fixed it (tag DOC), or every input that touched it agrees and no input raised an open question against it. Decisions tagged INF become binding when io accepts this BRD. [INF]

```yaml
locked:
  - {id: L-01, decision: "Parity invariant is handler equality, enforced by a per-stack CI check, not review", source: [DOC-5132058DFFAB, DOC-408DB108D7B9], tag: DOC}
  - {id: L-02, decision: "One versioned package per design area under @io-kit, pinned per stack; improvement = kit bump + one PR per stack; stacks deploy independently", source: [DOC-5132058DFFAB], tag: DOC}
  - {id: L-03, decision: "One capability manifest (caps.json) per MCP surface, generated by the adapter build from the governed handler registry, feeding nav, schema_form, parity and policy keys", source: [DOC-93597FD399C6, DOC-6F606A034072, DOC-3724FD572867, DOC-408DB108D7B9], tag: INF}
  - {id: L-04, decision: "Unwrapped action registry for Enceladus v2 and io-graph (per-action inputSchema/outputSchema/annotations/requiresGovernanceHash) is the first implementation dependency", source: [DOC-3724FD572867, DOC-18973FB09747, DOC-5132058DFFAB], tag: DOC}
  - {id: L-05, decision: "A registry-derived palette command that opens a generated schema_form counts as 'covered'; bespoke pages are UX, not parity", source: [DOC-6F606A034072], tag: INF}
  - {id: L-06, decision: "Authorization is server-only: authorize(principal, action, mode) in every governed handler; UI reads a PermissionManifest via can(); X-Io-Mode is a request, never a grant", source: [DOC-FB1738F8E0A2], tag: DOC}
  - {id: L-07, decision: "Token custody: memory + HttpOnly auth-edge cookie on every stack; nothing in localStorage; refresh failure -> 401 AUTH_REFRESH_FAILED", source: [DOC-D484594E8479, DOC-FB1738F8E0A2], tag: DOC}
  - {id: L-08, decision: "IdP-neutral core: an IdP is an IdpAdapter (cognito, keycloak, nextAuth); core never imports an IdP SDK", source: [DOC-FB1738F8E0A2], tag: DOC}
  - {id: L-09, decision: "Realtime carries signals only; data arrives via governed page/since handlers; AppSync Events is the transport (amends DOC-A5BCD6216666 WS default)", source: [DOC-256B5F36C6FD, DOC-A4F0A2A44AE2], tag: INF}
  - {id: L-10, decision: "Feed cursors are opaque, HMAC-signed, versioned; never expose LastEvaluatedKey; since() optional in 0.x, seq required by 1.0", source: [DOC-256B5F36C6FD], tag: INF}
  - {id: L-11, decision: "md = think's unified/react-markdown engine + Enceladus docstore semantics; rehype-sanitize; rawHtml never 'allow'", source: [DOC-488491DADD6C, DOC-C97D5B581CB4], tag: INF}
  - {id: L-12, decision: "ResolvedCall v1 (incl. governanceHash, principal, sideEffects) is the cross-surface dry-run contract; type owned by the kit, handlers conform", source: [DOC-3724FD572867, DOC-24F0950D339A], tag: INF}
  - {id: L-13, decision: "Recipe bindings compile to RFC 6901 pointers; no loops/wildcards in v1; definitions in docstore, runs in DynamoDB; governance_hash injected per segment, never authored", source: [DOC-BE6CCB537BCF, DOC-6E3844E7EBBD], tag: INF}
  - {id: L-14, decision: "Convergence-to-best-existing is in scope; every stage_2/stage_3 'improve beyond' item is out of scope for this program", source: [DOC-5132058DFFAB, DOC-0048EA99B6DD], tag: DOC}
  - {id: L-15, decision: "ai.vagamod.io keeps Keycloak; no migration to the shared Cognito pool. @io-kit/auth publishes a cognito-vs-keycloak parity matrix at minimum and, as the target, passes its contract tests against a Keycloak fixture including realm-per-tenant multi-tenancy, so vagamod can be hosted for external tenants (commercial beta candidate 2027)", source: ["io ruling 2026-10-10", DOC-FB1738F8E0A2, DOC-D484594E8479], tag: DOC}
```

## 4. Kit package architecture

For each concern, this section gives one recommendation and names the alternatives. [INF unless tagged]

```yaml
kit_architecture:
  home:
    recommendation: "one new repo 'io-kit' (pnpm workspaces), one package directory per area plus tokens and parity; owned by the devops project as the convergence program's code home"
    alternatives: ["package directories inside each stack's repo (rejected: no single conformance run)", "kit inside the enceladus repo (rejected: couples kit releases to the enceladus pipeline and governs all stacks from one product repo)"]
    note: "monorepo-vs-multirepo for the STACKS stays deferred and is not load-bearing [DOC: DOC-5132058DFFAB s3]; this choice is only about the kit"
  registry:
    recommendation: "private npm scope on AWS CodeArtifact; exit cost low because it speaks the npm protocol"
    source: "[DOC: DOC-93597FD399C6 D1, DOC-C97D5B581CB4 OD-1, DOC-A4F0A2A44AE2 D1, DOC-6F606A034072 D1, DOC-488491DADD6C OD-1]"
    alternatives: ["npm private org", "git tags (rejected: no semver resolution, no provenance)"]
    vagamod_note: "vagamod deploys from a different pipeline (DOC-5132058DFFAB s6); its CI needs a read-only CodeArtifact token minted per build (no long-lived token in repo)"
  packages:
    - "@io-kit/auth  (core, /react, /server, /testing)"
    - "@io-kit/shell (root types, /react, /next adapter)"
    - "@io-kit/tokens (DTCG 2025.10 source -> CSS vars, Tailwind 4 @theme, precompiled CSS bridge)"
    - "@io-kit/md (core, /react incl. KitMarkdownServer)"
    - "@io-kit/search (core hooks, /react components, /testing)"
    - "@io-kit/feed (core, /react, /appsync, /testing, /windows)"
    - "@io-kit/schema_form (registry, walker, widgets, /testing)"
    - "@io-kit/recipes (definition + validator, /react RecipeRunView, /server runner client)"
    - "@io-kit/gates (card model, /react inbox, /server decide helpers)"
    - "@io-kit/parity (CLI 'io-kit parity', caps.json and routes.yaml JSON Schemas)"
  versioning:
    recommendation: "independent semver per package via changesets; 0.x until two stacks consume it in production, then 1.0; breaking = major; inter-package deps as peer ranges (^) so a stack can pin each package separately"
    alternatives: ["lockstep single version for all ten (rejected: forces every stack to take every area's change)"]
    contract_versions: "wire contracts carry their own version independent of package semver (feed.vN schema field, SanitizePolicy.version, ResolvedCall v1, caps.json schemaVersion) [DOC: DOC-256B5F36C6FD s3.1, DOC-488491DADD6C s3; INF for caps.json]"
  release_and_propagation:
    recommendation: "merge to io-kit main -> changesets release -> publish with provenance -> bot opens one PR per consuming stack bumping the pin -> stack CI runs contract tests + parity check -> stack merges on its own cadence"
    rule: "a stack may lag at most one minor per package before its parity job warns; two minors fails [INF]"
  contract_tests:
    recommendation: "each package ships /testing: (a) conformance suites for server-side contracts (feed page/since/tombstone/gap; search response shape and degraded rules; auth error codes and manifest; schema_form ResolvedCall; gates decide/If-Match); (b) consumer fixtures recorded from each stack and replayed in kit CI on every PR, so a kit change that breaks one consumer fails before release"
    source: "[DOC: DOC-5132058DFFAB s6 coupling; DOC-A4F0A2A44AE2 s4 stage_2 conformance suite; DOC-FB1738F8E0A2 s3 /testing]"
    golden_corpora: "md golden tests on real 15-80 KB docstore docs [DOC: DOC-488491DADD6C s2]; parity golden on the baseline numbers [DOC: DOC-408DB108D7B9 s3]"
  consumer_pinning:
    recommendation: "exact versions in each stack's package.json (no ranges); lockfile committed; JS stacks (think, coach) consume via shipped .d.ts and JSDoc types"
    source: "[DOC: DOC-1C29BA594950 D2; DOC-6F606A034072 s4 think note]"
  css_strategy:
    recommendation: "tokens ship Tailwind 4 @theme; vagamod upgrades Tailwind 3->4 before shell adoption; precompiled CSS is a bridge only"
    source: "[DOC: DOC-93597FD399C6 D2, DOC-6F606A034072 D2]"
```

## 6. Per-stack migration sequencing
<!-- enc:block:01M4JCQGHSN5TZAAEZE70XSKK2 -->

**Reconciliation.** The Wave C docs give five different stack orders:
- auth: coach, enceladus, think, vagamod [DOC: DOC-FB1738F8E0A2 s4].
- shell: enceladus, think, coach, vagamod [DOC: DOC-6F606A034072 s4].
- md: kit, think, coach, vagamod, enceladus [DOC: DOC-488491DADD6C s4].
- search: enceladus, think, coach, vagamod [DOC: DOC-0048EA99B6DD s4].
- feed: coach, enceladus, think, vagamod [DOC: DOC-256B5F36C6FD s4].

The orders do not truly conflict. Each one ranks stacks within a single area, and areas are separate packages. What they lack is a cross-area order within each stack, plus a program-level priority. This BRD sets that priority as **parity first**. Dependencies between areas fix the order: auth's can() gates the shell, the shell palette opens schema_form, schema_form renders gate inputs and ResolvedCall, and recipes depend on both schema_form and gates [DOC: DOC-6E3844E7EBBD edges]. [INF]

**Overrides** [INF]:
- **O-1, search.** DOC-0048EA99B6DD s4 places coach third. This BRD moves coach search to "conditional, after vagamod". coach fronts no MCP surface (0/0 in DOC-408DB108D7B9 s3), so its migration adds no parity, and its backend (F-07) is undecided.
- **O-2, auth.** DOC-FB1738F8E0A2 s4 serializes think after Enceladus. This BRD lets think's auth run in parallel with Enceladus once coach has proven the core. think carries the largest parity gap (88 missing) and the localStorage custody risk, and it shares the Cognito pool. The added prerequisite is a think group claim.
- **O-3, area order.** No C doc ordered schema_form, recipes or gates across stacks. This BRD sets Enceladus first for all three, because it alone has server dry_run, the escalation gate type and the unwrapped registry dependency. think follows, then vagamod. (Amended by O-6: the enceladus backend stays the reference, but think's UI adopts before enceladus's.)
- **O-4, md.** DOC-488491DADD6C s4 keeps Enceladus last, and this BRD agrees. But the Enceladus docstore preset is pulled into E3 so that gates and recipes in E4 can render markdown prompts.
- **O-5, feed.** DOC-256B5F36C6FD s4 and DOC-A4F0A2A44AE2 D6 make the vagamod feed conditional. The BRD keeps that, and the parity diff decides; today vagamod's 12 actions include no feed.
- **O-6, stack order (io ruling 2026-10-10, L-16).** The program adopts the kit stack by stack in the order coach.thepup.io, think.thepup.io, enceladus.jreese.net, ai.vagamod.io. coach goes first as the modernization prelude to its platform BRD DOC-8EDA2CBF674E: it takes auth, feed, shell and md from the kit and runs the parity job green at 0/0, so a surface added by DOC-8EDA2CBF674E is covered from day one. think follows (largest gap, 88 missing). enceladus is third: its backend work (the L-04 registry, server dry_run, the escalation gate type) proceeds in E0 regardless and the kit's reference implementations are proven against enceladus handlers, but enceladus UI adoption follows think. vagamod is last and keeps Keycloak (L-15). Where O-2, O-3 or a per-area order above conflicts with this, L-16 wins; within a wave, coach work lands first, then think, enceladus, vagamod. [DOC: io]

## 9. Risks and mitigations

```yaml
risks:
  - {id: R-01, risk: "A kit bump breaks one stack and stalls all", source: "DOC-5132058DFFAB s6", mitigation: "exact pins per stack; consumer fixtures replayed in kit CI; one PR per stack merges independently", tag: DOC}
  - {id: R-02, risk: "Unwrapped registry slips and holds 129 actions at zero", source: "DOC-3724FD572867 s2", mitigation: "start in E0 in parallel with kit foundation; close vagamod and think's four schema-ready surfaces first so the check proves itself on 91 actions", tag: INF}
  - {id: R-03, risk: "vagamod handler equality impossible because MCP tools bypass REST handlers", source: "DOC-85B6774DAC96 via DOC-F5EF46453ABB", mitigation: "refactor both paths onto shared handler functions before E2; no waiver for this class", tag: INF}
  - {id: R-04, risk: "Generic forms are 'covered' but poor UX, so io still prefers agents", source: "L-05", mitigation: "track bespoke-page backlog separately; measure io's UI-vs-agent action share after E2", tag: INF}
  - {id: R-05, risk: "Scope creep into improve-beyond (search R1-R8, Cedar, durable functions)", source: "DOC-5132058DFFAB s6; DOC-0048EA99B6DD", mitigation: "L-14; E5 only after io re-scopes", tag: DOC}
  - {id: R-06, risk: "Enceladus md migration regresses the only production section editor", source: "DOC-488491DADD6C s4", mitigation: "golden corpus, old parser behind flag for one release", tag: DOC}
  - {id: R-07, risk: "AppSync auth cutover drops live subscriptions", source: "DOC-256B5F36C6FD s4", mitigation: "parallel Cognito namespace for one kit minor", tag: DOC}
  - {id: R-08, risk: "Write actions without dry_run executed from a form cause irreversible effects", source: "DOC-3724FD572867 s2, OD-F", mitigation: "typed confirm, counted in CI, tool_call gate for destructive actions from E4; annotation defaults are destructive=true", tag: INF}
  - {id: R-09, risk: "Docs and mandates describe rules the deployment does not enforce (known estate drift class)", source: "none in pack", mitigation: "parity check is a CI job with a committed baseline, not a policy statement; probe each check against a deliberately failing fixture", tag: INF}
  - {id: R-10, risk: "Shared Cognito pool tier not Essentials, blocking refresh rotation and stage-2 auth", source: "DOC-D484594E8479 D2, DOC-FB1738F8E0A2 D2", mitigation: "confirm tier in E0; stage-1 auth does not depend on it", tag: DOC}
  - {id: R-11, risk: "Inter-package peer ranges force lockstep bumps (shell->tokens, schema_form->md, recipes->schema_form/gates)", source: "VI-6", mitigation: "peer ranges ^major; contract-version fields decouple wire from package semver", tag: INF}
  - {id: R-12, risk: "Program cost: dispatch tokens near 95k per writer", source: "DOC-18973FB09747 s5", mitigation: "smaller packs, fewer tool calls, code tasks scoped to one package x one stack", tag: DOC}
```
